subject.title: [Feature] Queue prompts when API limits prevent an immediate response

question: Should OpenClaw add a core SQLite-backed capacity-wait prompt queue for prompts blocked by provider/model API limits, and how should that design coordinate with the open followup-recovery and cooldown PRs?
rationale: The remaining work is not a narrow patch because it changes persistent runtime state, provider retry semantics, user-visible waiting behavior, and which partial PR branches should be sponsored or replaced.

options.title: Sponsor durable capacity-wait queue
options.body: Design the queue as core SQLite state with replay, visibility, and provider cooldown semantics, then land or replace related PR slices only where they fit that design.

options.title: Narrow to restart followup persistence
options.body: Treat provider-limit auto-replay as a separate future decision and first land only durable followup queue recovery across gateway restarts.

options.title: Keep current cooldown behavior
options.body: Accept cooldown copy/session suspension as the intended behavior and close the broader automatic replay direction later with an explicit product decision.

recommendation.title: Sponsor durable capacity-wait queue
recommendation.body: Design the queue as core SQLite state with replay, visibility, and provider cooldown semantics, then land or replace related PR slices only where they fit that design.

likelyOwner.reason: Peter has the strongest sampled history across the queue, model-fallback, and cross-cutting runtime policy surfaces involved in this design choice.
